## 1. Reconstructing the profile formulation

Let y have period 2pi and let E_y denote normalized averaging. For a profile U(y) and profile velocity V(y), define

    L_B(U,V) = E_y [F(B+(V|U_y))-F(B)].                    (1.1)

A scalar functional P_B on smooth periodic profiles is called dominating if, for every compatible strip Phi on [0,T] x T,

    P_B(Phi(T,.))-P_B(Phi(0,.))
       <= integral_0^T L_B(Phi(x,.),Phi_x(x,.)) dx.       (1.2)

If P_B is differentiable along all smooth profile directions, its differential version is

    DP_B(U)[V] <= L_B(U,V)                                (1.3)

for every U,V. Integrating (1.3) implies (1.2); conversely short straight profile paths yield (1.3) when the derivatives and action are continuous. Closed paths eliminate the potential, so (1.2) proves Jensen at B. Existence of an unrestricted P_B is not assumed merely from rank-one convexity.

Write P=(Phi_x|0), Q=(0|Phi_y), and

    R_F(C,Z)=F(C+Z)-F(C)-DF(C)[Z].

Both P and Q have rank at most one. Direct subtraction gives

    F(B+P+Q)-F(B)
      = R_F(B+Q,P)+R_F(B,Q)+DF(B+Q)[P]+DF(B)[Q].          (1.4)

The final term averages to zero. The remaining linear term is the circulation of

    alpha_(F,B)(U)[V] = E_y DF(B+(0|U_y))[(V|0)].         (1.5)

Thus the prior identity is correct: it retains a joint signed circulation and two nonnegative rank-one remainders. Cancellation of polynomial circulation through degree three is sufficient for quartic Jensen, but is not automatic for profiles. A no-negative-cycle certificate on a fixed graph supplies (1.2) only for the tested transitions and does not address profiles outside that graph.

The full prior PROFILE_CIRCULATION.md was read. Its nine-group verifier was replayed successfully, including reconstruction of all 32,805 edge inequalities. The replay checks the inherited finite claims; it is not an independent analytic proof of any of the earlier long contact classifications. None of those classifications is a premise below.

This note extends incoming Theorem 2.1 from first transverse derivatives to
every fixed finite derivative order. It also checks the critical-trace and
concatenation arguments. No repository or supplied original was changed.

All profiles U,V are arbitrary C-infinity periodic maps T -> R^2, where T has
period 2*pi. Their means are NOT constrained. E denotes normalized y-average.
F:R^(2x2)->R is continuous and differentiable at the fixed background B. No
growth bound, rotational symmetry, homogeneity, convexity, or rank-one
convexity is required for the rigidity theorem. Smoothness of the storage
density means C-infinity on the whole finite-dimensional jet space.

The action and domination condition are

  L_B(U,V) = E [F(B+(V|U'))-F(B)],
  DP(U)[V] <= L_B(U,V)                         for every smooth U,V.  (D)

Equivalently, when the density is smooth, (D) is domination on all positive
duration smooth compatible strips, by the chain rule and short straight
profile paths. No limiting regularity of P on nonsmooth profiles is assumed.

THEOREM A: EVERY SMOOTH FINITE-JET DENSITY REDUCES TO FIRST ORDER

Fix an integer k>=1 and suppose

  P(U) = E p(U,U',...,U^(k)),

where p is smooth and satisfies (D). Then there are smooth A:R^2->R^2,
c:R^2->R and a smooth finite-jet H of order at most k-1 such that, identically
on the jet space,

  p(j^k U) = A(U).U' + c(U) + D_y H(j^(k-1)U).              (A1)

The last term integrates to zero for every smooth periodic U. Thus finite
higher derivatives do not enlarge the set of possible smooth local storage
functionals under universal domination.

Proof, step 1: a uniform L1 bound on the Euler derivative.

Write q_j=U^(j), with q_0=U, and let D be total y differentiation. The Euler
derivative of p is the smooth vector-valued differential expression

  e_p(j^(2k)U) = sum_(j=0)^k (-D)^j p_(q_j)(j^k U),
  DP(U)[V] = E e_p(j^(2k)U).V.                              (A2)

For R<infinity put

  M_R = max_(|q|<=R, |v|<=1) |F(B+(v|q))-F(B)| < infinity.

If ||U'||_infinity<=R, use the smooth test velocity

  V_eta(y) = e_p(y) / sqrt(|e_p(y)|^2+eta^2).

Its pointwise norm is <=1. Condition (D) gives E e_p.V_eta <= M_R. Let eta
decrease to zero, using dominated convergence for this fixed smooth U:

  E |e_p(j^(2k)U)| <= M_R.                                  (A3)

This is the crucial bound. It controls the Euler derivative independently
of ev

## 3. Main theorem and full proof

### Theorem 3.1

There is no real-linear map

    T: V9 -> {finite real-valued functionals on all smooth periodic profiles},
    F -> P_F,

with P_F(0)=0 for every F, such that (D) holds for every rank-one-convex F in V9.

There is no assumed full-profile regularity or transverse translation covariance.

### Step A: domination justifies averaging

Fix an F for which (D) holds and a smooth U. Write U_theta(y)=U(y+theta). For h nonzero connect U_theta to U_(theta+h) in width |h| by

    Phi(x,y)=U(y+theta+sgn(h)x), 0<=x<=|h|.

The columns are (sgn(h)U_y|U_y), evaluated at a translated argument. Hence the absolute action is at most |h|C(F,U), where

    C(F,U)=max_(sigma=+1,-1) E_y |F(sigma U_y|U_y)| < infinity.

Use domination for the path and its reverse. This gives

    |P_F(U_(theta+h))-P_F(U_theta)| <= C(F,U)|h|.          (3.1)

Thus every dominating functional is Lipschitz on every smooth transverse translation orbit. This does not imply continuity on weakly convergent high-frequency sequences.

Every f in V9 is a difference of convex quartics in V9. Let H(A)=|A|^4. Homogeneity gives a constant C_f with

    |D^2 f(A)[R,R]| <= C_f |A|^2 |R|^2,
    D^2 H(A)[R,R] = 8(A:R)^2+4|A|^2|R|^2.

For sufficiently large M, MH+f and MH are convex, and f=(MH+f)-MH. By linearity, P_f also has a Lipschitz translation orbit. Therefore the following integral exists for every f, without any additional regularity hypothesis:

    bar P_f(U)=(1/(2pi)) integral_0^(2pi) P_f(U_theta) dtheta. (3.2)

This map remains real-linear and normalized, and is transverse-translation invariant. For rank-one-convex F, apply (D) to every transverse translate of a strip and integrate in theta. The action is translation invariant, so bar P_F remains dominating.

It suffices to prove this averaged linear map vanishes.

### Step B: reflection-even components vanish

For each real t, define the convex quartic

    R_t(X|Y)=|X+tY|^4=(u+2tw+t^2v)^2.                    (3.3)

Let U,W be arbitrary smooth profiles. Choose a smooth path psi(s,y), 0<=s<=1, from U to W; straight interpolation suffices. For T>0 take the genuinely compatible strip

    Phi_T(x,y)=psi(x/T,y-tx), 0<=x<=T.

Its columns satisfy Phi_x+t Phi_y=T^(-1)psi_s. Averaged storage ignores the endpoint's transverse translation, so

    bar P_(R_t)(W)-bar P_(R_t)(U)
      <= T^(-3) integral_0^1 E_y |psi_s
